newsitem.title: INDIA: Cost of 1st half '97 rupee borrowings up - India IDBI.
newsitem.headline: Cost of 1st half '97 rupee borrowings up - India IDBI.

text.p: India's largest term lender, the Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI), said on Thursday its marginal cost of rupee borrowings had gone up in the first half of 1996/97 (April-March) as compared to the previous year.
"The marginal cost of rupee borrowings during the half year was significantly higher at 15.9 percent compared to 15.0 percent during the same period last year," it said in a statement.
The IDBI raised 60 billion rupees by way of borrowings between April and September, the statement said.
Rupee borrowings which comprised 85 percent of the resources raised were through certificates of deposit and privately placed bonds, it said.
The Indian government had approved a foreign currency limit of $550 million for 1996/97 for IDBI, of which it had already raised $330 million.

IDBI said its net profit would have been higher but for the impact of the loss of interest income of 200 million rupees due to non-utilisation of excess subscription received for one of its bond issues earlier this year.
Higher depreciation, particularly on account of leased assets also restricted the net profit, it said.
IDBI's net worth stood at 69.37 billion rupees end September 1996, with equity of 6.59 billion and reserves and surplus of 62.78 billion.
Total assets at 465.31 billion rupees showed a growth of 14 percent over the September 1995 figure, it said.
